messages:
carlos: Hey team — customer reported a big jump in latency and hosted billing today. Their app is pinned to our dedicated eu-west pool but traces show traffic egressing to hosted/us-east and some requests timing out (~2.2s extra). Can we triage? They say it started around 10:15 UTC.

maya: Thanks Carlos. Can you paste a sample request_id and the policy config for that customer? Also want the tenant's pin config (pin_region / pin_ttl) if available.

carlos: request_id=req_0a9f4e2b; here is the pin snippet from their dashboard (sanitized):
```
customer_id: C-1987
pin: { region: "eu-west", pool: "dedicated-eu-1", ttl_seconds: 3600, fallback: "allow_hosted" }
```
Full trace: https://traces.internal/reports/req_0a9f4e2b (link to internal)

lena: Looking at routing logs for req_0a9f4e2b: it matched dedicated-eu-1 but then we saw an immediate re-route to hosted-us-east with reason="capacity_shortfall". There's a note in the runtime: "evicted_from_pool: unable_to_start_container".

ravi: Two quick hypotheses: 1) the dedicated pool lost capacity (OOM/crash) and autoscaler didn't bring up replacements in-region quickly, so fallback kicked in. 2) There's a bug where pin_ttl expiry + concurrent requests triggers fallback even though node(s) still healthy.

carlos: Customer insists their dedicated dashboard shows GPUs healthy at 10:14. They have a short spike in qps (~2.5x). They were on a canary rollout of a model upgrade during that window.

maya: Can we repro locally? If pinned pool spikes and some requests are queued, does the policy immediately spill to hosted? Need exact repro steps so we can tell customer what happened and whether to compensate billing.

lena: Repro steps I used:
1) Create a dedicated pool with 2 nodes in eu-west, pin customer with fallback=allow_hosted, ttl=3600.
2) Simulate 3x qps burst for 30s that saturates model load.
3) Observe routing decisions via `rcli events tail --customer C-1987`
Expected: queue + autoscale. Observed: first few excess reqs routed to hosted (cross-region).
Command I ran:```
# simulate burst
loadgen --target qps 180 --model redwood-13b --region eu-west --customer C-1987
```

ravi: Important note: hosted reroutes are billed as hosted usage. That explains the billing spike. Also cross-region adds latency (eu->us) which matches the 2s delta Carlos reported.

maya: Do we have logs showing why autoscale didn't kick? lena?

lena: Autoscaler shows scale event scheduled but container start failed twice due to image fetch timeout to our eu registry (repo-edge). There's a transient network failure to the registry at 10:14:22. So autoscale couldn't replace nodes fast enough and fallback policy immediate->hosted fired.

carlos: Ugh. Customer asks for root cause and credits for hosted charges. They also want a way to avoid cross-region fallback while still allowing some burst handling.

ravi: Mitigations: 1) change fallback to "queue_until_capacity" or "retry-local" for critical customers. 2) increase min_capacity on dedicated pool to handle x1.5 spikes. 3) fix registry transient: infra team already firing a P1 incident for repo-edge.

lena: Temporary hotfix we can toggle per-customer: set `fallback: "strict_local_queue"` which will cause requests to be queued for up to 60s instead of immediate hosted fallback. Patch config API:```
PATCH /v1/customers/C-1987/pin
{ "fallback": "strict_local_queue" }
```
This will prevent hosted billing but may increase client-side latency if queue time > client timeout.

maya: Action items:
- lena: push the patch to set fallback to strict_local_queue for C-1987 now (with customer consent).
- ravi: confirm hosted billing usage and calculate credits for the extra hosted tokens; recommend a credit proposal.
- infra-bot: open incident for eu registry outage and include timeline.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-eu-registry-01 with priority P1. Start time 2026-02-12T10:14:05Z.

lena: Patch applied for C-1987. I've set fallback->strict_local_queue and increased min_capacity from 2->3 while we validate. I also added a temporary rule to prefer local region: `prefer_local_region: true` in routing config.

ravi: I'll run a billing audit and propose credits. Early estimate: ~48k tokens routed to hosted during spike -> suggest 50% credit given transient autoscaler/registry failure.

maya: Carlos, can you relay the mitigation and proposed credit to the customer? Offer status update: registry incident, we've applied conservative pin settings and increased min_capacity; we recommend they keep fallback strict_local_queue for now or increase min_capacity if they expect more bursts.

carlos: Noted. I'll send the update and ask if they want us to revert fallback after the issue is resolved. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

lena: Follow-up: we'll add a small runtime guard to avoid immediate hosted fallback if autoscaler has a pending scale-up within last 30s. I'll open a small PR and mark for hotpatch if repo-edge is risky.

ravi: One more thing — add this customer to the dedicated escalation runbook so ops knows to call them before making changes: contact ops-runbook entry C-1987.

maya: Closing loop: next update after infra confirms registry restored and billing audit complete.
